label: Modal spine stage one: necessary concrete individual from inert emptiness, with rivals recorded
summary: Owner-selected working root: God exists (stage 1), with a modal contingency argument as the first spine (docs/notes/modal-spine.md). Target of this attempt: stage one, a necessary concrete individual. The existing LocalFramePossibleExternalCause.necessaryConcrete route rests on the causal-opportunity premise, and the existing ExternalCandidateNecessity equivalence shows that premise already contains the possibility of a necessary concrete individual: the totality-cause relation does no logical work. This attempt replaces it by two temporally structured premises on the existing TemporalHistory.History: inert emptiness (a moment with nothing concrete present is followed only by such moments, in every history) and the possibility of a history with a moment free of contingent concrete individuals before a moment containing one. With the existing presence-to-existence contract and Euclidean plus actual-reflexive access, InertEmptiness.necessaryConcrete derives the existing NecessaryConcreteAt for the same rigid individual; no causal, grounding or explanatory relation is used. Controls: omitting inert emptiness (a beginning out of nothing), the possible contingent-free past (an initial state populated from its earliest moment) or presence-to-existence each lets the conclusion fail with the rest retained; a fourth interpretation jointly satisfies the bundle. Omission of the frame conditions is not tested. The two rivals are recorded as alternative_to statements so the premises can later be defended. Relation to earlier work: EmptyHistoryCausalAvailability reaches the same node through a causal-availability premise on negative facts and an empty contingent-bearer world; the present route uses no fact causation and no empty world, only empty moments. Rejected reading: deriving the causal-opportunity premise itself from inert emptiness, which is impossible without a causal relation; the new route bypasses that premise instead of discharging it. No premise is established and the root is not closed.
blocker: Both new premises are OPEN. Inert emptiness quantifies over every history of the frame and is silent about a first state with no earlier moment; the initial-state rival denies the possible contingent-free past. Stage two: the existing NecessaryConcreteUnderived argument carries the conclusion to a necessary concrete individual without an actual supporter of its being, under two further OPEN premises (supporters of necessary concreta are necessary; that support is well-founded), with no rival recorded for either. Whether that individual is the root the existing NecessaryClassicalGodRoot chain starts from is unchecked.
